# Sappurisa Sutta (MN 113 (PTS MN iii 37))

**ID:** MN 113 (PTS MN iii 37)
**Section:** Majjhimanikāya (mn)
**Collection:** Suttas-Early-1
**Title (Pali):** Sappurisa Sutta
**Title (English, from literature):** A True Person
**PTS:** MN iii 37
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/s0203m.mul1.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Sappurisa Sutta* ("A True Person" or "The True Man") is the 113th discourse of the *Majjhima Nikāya* (PTS MN iii 37) [Ñāṇamoli & Bodhi 1995]. In this discourse, the Buddha distinguishes the character of an untrue person from that of a true person, explaining that a truly good person does not disparage others or feel conceited and superior on account of their attainments or qualities [Ñāṇamoli & Bodhi 1995; Anālayo 2014]. The text sets out a detailed list of spiritual and ascetic qualities, meditative states, and attainments in relation to which conceit is to be avoided, including being learned, knowing the discourses, and knowing the Vinaya [Anālayo 2014]. In dealing with progressive meditative stages, the sutta explains that the training enables a practitioner to hold aloof (*atammayo*) and shed all tendencies toward imaginings or conceiving (*maññanā* / *maññati*), continuing up through the cessation of perception and feeling (*saññāvedayitanirodha-samāpatti*) [Ñāṇananda 1971; Shulman 2010].

Direct parallels to MN 113 are found in the Chinese Āgamas: MĀ 85 (titled the *Scripture of the True Man*, *Chen jen ching*), an individual translation cataloged as Taishō 48 (*Sat-puruṣa-sūtra*), and EĀ 17.9 [Tsukamoto 1979; Hahn et al. 1997]. While the Pāli text and T 48 warn against pride in being learned in the discourses and Vinaya, MĀ 85 adds the study of Abhidharma to this list [Anālayo 2014]. DharmaNexus confirms extensive cross-language alignments with MĀ (ZH_T01_0026) as well as shared passages in the Sarvāstivāda *Dharmaskandha* and Harivarman's *Satyasiddhiśāstra* [DharmaNexus]. Pali-internal reuse is most notable with the *Catukkanipāta* (AN 4), *Mahāparinibbāna Sutta* (DN 16), and adjacent suttas such as *Cūḷapuṇṇama Sutta* (MN 110) and *Apaṇṇaka Sutta* (MN 60) [DharmaNexus].
